title: Germany news: IG Metall union calls for new 24-hour strike
summary: Germany's biggest single union, IG Metall, is calling on car and shipyard workers to strike amid a pay row. Meanwhile, Germany's president is setting off on an Africa trip. DW has more.

image.caption: IG Metall has already called numerous strikes, as here in Sindelfingen in September [FILE: September 21, 2026]Image: Marijan Murat/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: IG Metall calls warning strike for Monday

blocks.caption: Germany's largest union is demanding ​a 5% ‌wage hike [FILE: September 2026]Image: Christophe Gateau/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: The powerful IG Metall union said on Sunday it would call another 24-hour strike on Monday as a pay dispute continues.

Altogether, some 23,000 workers at 19 companies in northern Germany have been called upon to participate, including employees at automaker Mercedes-Benz, shipbuilding company Meyer Werft and wind ​energy company Siemens Gamesa.
The union said that a strike on Friday saw some 12,300 workers walk out at 17 facilities.
It says that the strikes are meant to increase the pressure on employers to yield to its demands, which include a 5% ‌wage increase.
So far, employers have ⁠offered a one-off payment next year and a 1.3% wage increase from July 2028.
